_comment: Accepted pnpm-audit exceptions — task-prod-runtime-vulns (2026-08-16/17, round 3 per security-review PR #536); round 4 (2026-09-02, infra/audit-undici-advisories) added the @xmldom/xmldom group below. Read scripts/devops/check-pnpm-audit.mjs's module doc before editing. Every group below is keyed by exact GHSA id (not just a package name) — a NEW advisory id for an already-listed package is NOT covered and will gate CI red until it is triaged and either fixed or added here with its own reason. Every group MUST carry a `reason` of meaningful length (enforced by the guard, not just convention) — an empty or placeholder reason makes the guard treat the whole group as unaccepted regardless of severity. Round 2: vite/postcss/nanoid/@babel/core/js-yaml/qs/brace-expansion were ALL genuinely fixed (not just documented) after security-review found the earlier 'no fix below a major' reasons factually wrong for several of them — dependency bump + `pnpm dedupe`, or a root pnpm.overrides entry, none crossing a version-pins.md pin. Round 3: `esbuild` (round 2's remaining exception) is ALSO genuinely fixed now — a naive blanket `esbuild` override broke `pnpm build` (Vite's OWN internal esbuild@0.25.12 dependency, itself never vulnerable to either GHSA, conflicts with a forced newer version underneath it), but a SELECTOR override scoped to only the two actually-vulnerable consumers (`"tsx>esbuild"`, `"@esbuild-kit/core-utils>esbuild"` in root package.json) resolves both without ever touching Vite's own untouched, unaffected esbuild edge. Round 4: the gate went red again on `main` from FOUR newly-published advisories against packages that already had a pnpm.overrides floor from earlier rounds (qs >=6.15.2, fastify ^5.12.0, fast-uri >=3.1.5) — the floor itself hadn't moved since it was set, but newer CVEs raised the bar above it. All three were genuinely fixed by tightening the existing override floor (qs >=6.16.0, fastify ^5.12.1, fast-uri >=3.1.6 — still inside the ^5.8.5 fastify pin, no pin crossed); a fourth advisory (@xmldom/xmldom) was deliberately NOT fixed the same way — see its own group below for why. `pnpm --filter @crm/web build` before/after: identical PWA precache (99 entries, 3700.99 KiB) — none of the touched packages reach the shipped SPA bundle.

exceptions.reason: npm package `undici` is reachable ONLY through apps/web's devDependency chain vitest -> jsdom -> undici (jsdom's fetch/WebSocket polyfill for the jsdom Vitest test environment). Verified with `pnpm why undici -r`: zero paths through apps/api, zero paths through any apps/web PRODUCTION dependency — jsdom is a devDependency, never bundled by Vite for the shipped SPA (jsdom is Node-only and is not imported by any apps/web/app/** source file). Security-review (PR #536, round 2) independently confirmed this with a stronger method: a full production-dependency closure computed straight from the lockfile, not just `pnpm why`. apps/api does not depend on the undici npm package AT ALL. EVERY apps/api outbound `fetch()` call site (verified exhaustively, not a sample): finance/nbu-currency.service.ts (NBU exchange rate), finance/etherscan.service.ts (blockchain deposit/tx verification), job-sourcing/dou.provider.ts (DOU vacancy scraping), vacancies/turnstile.service.ts (Cloudflare Turnstile captcha verification), vacancies/google-indexing.service.ts (Google Indexing API), resumes/resume-ai.service.ts (Cloudflare Workers AI resume extraction), contact/resend-mailer.service.ts (Resend transactional email), and auth/auth.service.ts's TWO calls — the OAuth authorization-code-for-token exchange (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`) and the OIDC userinfo lookup (`https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`), the most sensitive pair in this whole list since they carry the session-issuing credential exchange — all use Node's built-in global `fetch()`, which is powered by Node 20's OWN internal bundled undici (`process.versions.undici == '6.13.0'` on the pinned Node 20 image) — a wholly separate artifact from the npm package pnpm audit is reporting on here, and OUTSIDE every one of these advisories' documented vulnerable range (all start at >=7.0.0; Node's internal copy is major version 6). Two further apps/api outbound egress paths do not go through `fetch()`/undici AT ALL, as a second independent line of defence even if the reasoning above were ever wrong: google-auth-library's own ID-token verification (auth.service.ts) resolves to `gaxios@7.1.5` -> `node-fetch@3.3.2` (confirmed via `pnpm why gaxios --filter @crm/api` / `pnpm why node-fetch --filter @crm/api` — real, separate production dependencies, not undici); and `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (documents/s3.service.ts, R2/S3 object storage) ships its own HTTP client stack, independent of both fetch() and the npm undici package. Fix path that would close this for good: bump apps/web's `jsdom` devDependency 29.1.1 -> 30.0.1 (jsdom@30 pulls undici ^8.9.0, patched) -- a MAJOR version bump of a test-only tool, deliberately deferred to a follow-up PR so this security-fix PR does not also have to revalidate every jsdom-reliant unit test in apps/web.

`@xmldom/xmldom` reaches apps/api production code through exactly one path: `mammoth` (DOCX -> plain-text extraction for uploaded resumes, apps/api/src/resumes/resume-text-extraction.service.ts). Verified with `pnpm why @xmldom/xmldom -r`: a single production edge, apps/api -> mammoth -> @xmldom/xmldom, no other consumer anywhere in the workspace. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6 is a SERIALIZATION-side defect: `Document.createEntityReference()` accepted an invalid XML Name, and `XMLSerializer.serializeToString()` under `{ requireWellFormed: true }` did not reject it when re-emitting the entity reference — i.e. it is only reachable by code that BUILDS an EntityReference node (typically from attacker-controlled data) and then SERIALIZES it back out with that flag. Read mammoth's own xmldom wrapper (node_modules/.../mammoth/lib/xml/xmldom.js): it calls `new xmldom.DOMParser().parseFromString()` and nothing else — mammoth only PARSES the DOCX XML to walk the resulting DOM and extract text/HTML; it never calls `XMLSerializer`, never calls `createEntityReference()`, never serializes anything back out. A repo-wide grep for `xmldom` outside node_modules (apps/api/src, apps/web/src) turns up only resume-text-extraction.service.ts, resume-render-responsiveness.spec.ts, sandboxed-process.ts, resume-source.util.ts and resume-fixtures.ts — every one of them talks to `mammoth`'s extraction API, never to `@xmldom/xmldom`'s own exports directly. The vulnerable call shape (build an EntityReference from untrusted input, serialize it with requireWellFormed) does not exist anywhere in this application. DELIBERATELY NOT bumped to the patched 0.8.15 in this same PR even though it is a same-line, override-free `pnpm update` (mammoth's own declared range `^0.8.6` already covers it): 0.8.15's changelog bundles an UNRELATED fix in the same release (GHSA-8344-3jmq-59r6 — attribute de-duplication during parsing moved from O(M^2) to O(M)) that happens to be the EXACT performance characteristic two existing regression tests use as their whole mechanism — resume-text-extraction.service.spec.ts's 'contains an expensive document no budget can see' (zip-bomb guard) and resume-render-responsiveness.spec.ts's 'keeps the API answering during extraction' both construct a many-attributes DOCX fixture explicitly BECAUSE 'xmldom's attribute handling is quadratic per element' (their own comments) and assert on the resulting ~3.4s/~18s parse time. Reproduced: bumping to 0.8.15 flips both from a real assertion to an instant 'resolved' — not flaky, 100% reproducible, confirmed against the upstream CHANGELOG.md entry for 0.8.15. Fixing that is a test-file change (AutoTest's zone-of-write, not DevOps's) and is out of scope for a dependency-audit PR that should not also have to re-derive those two fixtures' timing assumptions. Fix path: bump `@xmldom/xmldom` to >=0.8.15 in a follow-up PR that in the SAME change updates both fixtures above to a mechanism that does not depend on the now-fixed quadratic behavior.
